passage: Thursday night in the hostel common room, three friends and one visitor had their laptops open. Varun read out a message from his professor: she wanted to talk about his essay, because parts of it sounded machine-written. His stomach dropped. Two paragraphs had been drafted by a chatbot and then tidied by him, so he decided to bring his notes and chat history to the meeting and ask what the department allowed. Jahnavi barely looked up. She was typing to her AI companion about a rotten day, and it answered warmly every time, never tired, never critical. "Easier than ringing anyone," she said, then added, "though I haven't replied to Nisha in two weeks." Yusuf pasted a chatbot's summary of a tax rule into his slides. "It sounds so sure," he said, then frowned. "I'll find the real source before I present." From the sofa, Ritu scrolled job listings for her design course and read one aloud that mentioned automation. "Will there be any work for me at all?" she asked. 😟

qa.q: What did Varun's professor say about his essay?
qa.a: The professor said parts of it sounded machine-written and wanted to talk about it.

qa.q: How do Varun's plan for the meeting and Yusuf's plan for his slides show a similar careful approach to AI tools?
qa.a: Both take responsibility for what the AI produced: Varun will bring his notes and chat history and be honest about his process, while Yusuf will look for the real source instead of accepting a confident answer.

qa.q: What was Varun feeling when he read the professor's message, and how can you tell?
qa.a: He felt exposed and anxious; his stomach dropped, and he quickly began planning what to bring to the meeting.

qa.q: What could Jahnavi do to keep her human friendships growing alongside her companion?
qa.a: She could reply to Nisha and arrange to talk or meet, enjoying the companion's comfort without letting it replace her friends. 🙂

grounding: Four students at one hostel table show different stances toward AI tools: suspicion from a professor, comfort from a companion, over-trust of confident answers, and fear about jobs.
